Proposition
[Classification of hyperbolic-plane isometries] 1. Proposition 4.9.3\group foliations Source: thurston:page-0078, thurston:page-0079 Every nontrivial orientation-preserving isometry of $\HH ^2$ is exactly one of elliptic (one interior fixed point), hyperbolic (one invariant geodesic), or parabolic (one boundary fixed point). The centralizer of each such isometry is abelian.

Proof

\sketch Bisectors of successive segments $x,gx,g^2x$ either meet, have a common perpendicular, or meet at infinity; these alternatives give the three types and their uniqueness. The invariant-point or invariant-axis description makes the centralizer abelian.

□
